Yes, that's the behavior I expect. With the **javascript** label still lit up, typing "guides" narrowed the two javascript links down to just **JavaScript | MDN** — because that's the one whose text mentions guides. The label and the search working together like that, each one tightening things further, is exactly how I'd want to zero in on something.

And your assumptions match mine:

- Searching across the title, the description, and the source name all at once is right — I don't always remember which of those a word was in.
- Not caring about capital letters is important. I'd never want to miss a result just because I typed "guides" instead of "Guides."
- And keeping the label selected while I search is the whole point — I don't want typing to throw away the category I already picked.

One thing tied to this that I'll mention now since we're on search: eventually I'll be jotting my own little notes on some bookmarks, and when that exists I'd want the search to look inside those notes too, so I can find a link by something I wrote about it. Not asking you to build it this second — just so search is designed with that in mind.

For what you're showing here, the combined narrowing is right.
